helpIntro: Windows 10/11 x64 · No Node.js installation needed · Official Discord user app
helpCreateBody: Create an app in Developer Portal. Enable User Install and Guild Install under Installation. User Install scope: applications.commands. Guild Install scopes: bot + applications.commands; permission: Create Expressions only. Leave privileged intents and Requires OAuth2 Code Grant off, and Interactions Endpoint URL empty.
helpEnvBody: Get the Bot Token from the Bot page (reset it yourself if needed). Click Open env configuration, paste the token after DISCORD_TOKEN=, then save. Do not prefix it with Bot or share it. Normally leave OWNER_ID and TARGET_GUILD_ID empty: the owner is detected automatically and /setup binds the server. Click Start service and wait for connected status.
helpInstallBody: Once connected, click Add to my apps and Add to target server and complete both Discord authorizations. Choose your own private server as the target. The bot only joins that target. Run /setup in it and wait for the bound confirmation. No browser extension or modified Discord client is required.
helpUseBody: Right-click a message containing custom emojis → Apps → Save Emoji. For multiple emojis, select items then click outside the menu to submit. A single emoji saves immediately. Use the target server’s emoji picker afterward. Menus show at most 25 emojis; repeated saves use extra slots. Stickers and Unicode emojis are unsupported.
helpBoundaryBody: Saving does not replace Nitro. Sending emojis to other servers still requires Nitro / Nitro Basic and external emoji permission. Source servers do not need the bot, but Discord restrictions on user apps still apply. Missing commands: finish both installs and reload Discord. Failures: check token, network, permissions and emoji slots; retry later after rate limits. Closing the window keeps the tray running; quitting, shutdown or disconnection prevents saving. Enable and save the startup checkbox to launch after Windows sign-in.
